newsitem.title: EGYPT: PRESS DIGEST - Egypt economic press - April 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Egypt economic press - April 13.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian economic press this week. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Capital Market Authority is considering replacing the five percent ceiling and floor for stock prices within the next few months. Analysts and observers welcome the suggestion.
- Arab African International Bank bond issue ended 1.04 times oversubscribed, an official at agents National Bank of Egypt, said.
- Commercial International Bank is expected to sign next Friday a syndicated loan agreement for $150 million to $200 million over a period of three years.

- Abu Qir Fertiliser and Chemicals said its net after-tax profits for the first nine-months of the 1996/7 financial year rose 29 percent to 184.46 million pounds ($54.34 million) from 142.98 million in the same period of the previous year. Net sales were 452.07 million compared to 407.48 million in the same year ago period. The company's most important project is a urea plant under construction which will have a 600,000 tonne annual production and which is expected to cost 1.1 billion pounds.

- Mamdouh el Kholi, chairman of Suez Cement, told the stock exchange board that the firm's unaudited pre-tax profits for calendar 1996 were 297.149 million pounds compared to 293.060 million in 1995. The dividend and shareholder's portion of this profit will be decided in the firm's general assembly which will be held at the end of April.

- Holding Company for Agricultural Development is planning to privatise 20 to 30 percent of its stake in Nubariya Agricultural Engineering and Mechanisation at an expected prices of 24 to 26 pounds per share. The offer will probably take place within the next two weeks. The firm made after-tax profits for the six months ending December 31 of 1.385 million pounds from 1.098 million in the same year ago period.

- Paints and Chemical Industries/PACHIN made net after-tax profits for the eight months ending February of 59 million pounds compared to 53 million in the same period of the previous year. Sales were at 177 million down from 182 million.
- Kafr el-Zayat Pesticides and Chemicals made net pre-tax profits of 10.750 million in the first eight months of the financial year 1996/7, compared to 2.255 million in the same year ago period.

- Cabinet approves the public offering of up to 40 percent of Alexandria Flour Mills. The firm made net after-tax profits worth 16.144 million in the period ending December 31, 1996 compared to 9.9 million in the same year ago period.
- Shares offered in Alexandria Maritime and Commercial Bank .
- Prices of most shares are steady and fluctuations have decreased.

- Egyptian Financial and Industrial is forecast to increase net profits for 1996/7 to 65 million pounds from 25.04 million in the previous year. Sales are also expected to be higher at 310 million from 173.22 million.
- Industrial Development Bank issues bonds worth 150 million pounds. Credit Foncier Egyptien to issue bonds worth 40 million.
